chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, who said: My brother Ja'far ibn Isa narrated to me, saying:

I asked Al-Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fasting of Ashura and what people say about it. He said: The fasting of Ibn Marjanah is what you are asking me about. It is a day that the claimants from the family of Ziyad fasted for the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). It is a day that the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) consider unlucky, and the people of Islam consider unlucky. The day that Islam and its people consider unlucky is not fasted and is not blessed. Monday is a day in which Allah took His Prophet (peace be upon him), and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) were afflicted only on Monday, so we considered it unlucky, but our enemies considered it blessed. On the day of Ashura, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, and Ibn Marjanah considered it blessed, and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) consider it unlucky. So whoever fasts them or considers them blessed will meet Allah, Almighty and Majestic, with a changed heart, and his gathering place will be with those who instituted their fasting and considered them blessed.

key_terms.ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ: Ibn Marjanah, a Umayyad governor known for celebrating the martyrdom of Al-Husayn
key_terms.مَحْشَرُهُ: His gathering place (on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.يَتَشَأَّمُ: To consider unlucky or take as an omen of misfortune

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Al-Rida advise against fasting on Ashura and what is the significance of Ibn Marjanah?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the Umayyad practice of fasting on Ashura was a deliberate act of celebration for Imam Al-Husayn’s martyrdom, contrasting it with the Prophet’s fasting on Mondays, which commemorated his birth and the Ahl al-Bayt’s tribulations. This hadith highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'Tashauum' (considering a day unlucky) versus 'Tabarruk' (seeking blessing), warning that those who fast Ashura align themselves with the Umayyads and will be resurrected with a 'changed heart' (Masukh al-Qalb).
